actors: The distributor making the promotional offer.
The client to whom the benefit is offered.
The person funding or fulfilling the benefit, if different from the distributor; its identity must be established from the offer evidence.
The fund house whose identity may define the promoted product type.
classification_assumptions: The restriction attaches to a distributor's act of offering a gift. The quoted text does not additionally require the distributor to fund or fulfil it.
Separately identifiable benefit components are assessed separately; boundaries require judgment where benefits cannot reliably be separated.
Gift status requires substantive assessment. Guaranteed returns and other incentives are not automatically gifts merely because paragraph 9 says they may be considered gifts.
The fee or charge discount exception applies to the assessed component itself, not every benefit packaged with a discount.
Product-type promotion includes funds identified by fund type or fund house.
The words 'should not offer' are modeled as a prohibition under this selected restriction, without determining criminal liability or granting legal approval.

How is the component linked to a specific investment product or a particular product type?

The individual benefit component being offered.
Any separate funding or fulfilment undertaking for that component.
The specific investment product or particular product type promoted.
The actual fund return, distinguished from an additional top-up return.
The identifiable fees or charges allegedly discounted.

citations.quote: Paragraph 3.11 of the Code of Conduct provides that distributors should not offer any gifts (other than a discount of fees or charges) in promoting a specific investment product or a particular type of investment product to a client.

If gifts are offered in such a way that they are linked to a particular type of investment product, such as certain types of funds or funds offered by certain fund houses, then such gifts will be bound by this requirement as investors may be distracted from the unique features and risks of such particular funds3.

Even where the guaranteed returns offered would not constitute a “structured product” under the SFO, distributors are reminded to have regard to paragraph 3.11 of the Code of Conduct in offering such returns or other incentives in promoting SFC-authorised funds, as they may be considered a gift that should not be offered to investors.

Typically, the “guaranteed returns” in such cases comprise: (i) the actual return of the relevant fund(s) invested by the investor (ie, fund return); and (ii) a top-up return to make up the difference between the fund return and the guaranteed rate of return offered by the distributor.

reading.distinction: The prior component model abstraction.ea48395ee1fc075eb75b04b4 describes the distributor as the provider and places provider_is_distributor in scope. If 'provider' means the funder or fulfiller, that vocabulary can exclude a gift offered by a distributor but supplied by another person. This proposal separates offering from funding and fulfilment. It is a consequential correction to that possible narrowing, while remaining compatible with abstraction.933486dc69f18e0075717cc1's offeror-based scope. Neither third-party funding nor any actual third-party arrangement is assumed.

facts.meaning: The actor making the assessed offer acts as a distributor in this promotional context, independently of who funds or fulfils the benefit.
facts.name: offeror_is_distributor

facts.meaning: The assessed actor offers this benefit component to the identified client at the assessment time. Attribution of the offer must be established; funding, fulfilment, acceptance and payment are not prerequisites for this fact.
facts.name: actor_offers_component_to_client
facts.unit: Boolean offering relation for one actor, component, client and time

facts.meaning: The assessed component is substantively classified as a gift under the quoted restriction, separately from the discount exception. Its being a guaranteed return or incentive alone does not establish this classification.
facts.name: component_is_gift
facts.unit: Boolean classification of one benefit component

facts.meaning: The assessed component itself constitutes a discount of identifiable fees or charges. A discount in another component does not satisfy this fact.
facts.name: component_is_fee_or_charge_discount
facts.unit: Boolean exception classification of one benefit component

facts.meaning: Offering this component promotes an identified specific investment product to the client.
facts.name: component_promotes_specific_product

facts.meaning: Offering this component is linked to promoting a particular type of investment product, including certain fund types or funds offered by certain fund houses.
facts.name: component_promotes_product_type

reading.statement: [TRUE_IS_PROHIBITED] Within distributor scope, the result answers whether this actor's offering of this component to this client falls within the selected gift prohibition. True means the actor offers a gift that is not itself a fee or charge discount and has the specified product or product-type promotional connection, irrespective of who funds or fulfils it. False means that conjunction is not met for this component; it does not approve the combined offer. Unknown facts remain unknown unless other inputs determine the expression.
reading.subject: Attribution of the gift offer separately from funding or fulfilment

relationships: The distributor offers a component to the client; another person's funding or fulfilment, if present, is a separate relationship.
Funding or fulfilment alone does not establish who made the promotional offer.
The component belongs to a combined offer but has its own gift and discount classifications.
The component may promote a specific product, a product type, or both.
A fund house can identify the promoted product type without being the offeror.
Actual fund return and additional top-up return are distinguished before classifying benefits.
Structured-product classification is separate from application of the gift restriction.
proposals.temporal_basis: Assess attribution, component terms and promotional linkage when the component is offered. Later funding or fulfilment is not a stated prerequisite. Effective dates and transitional provisions are not supplied.
proposals.unit_of_assessment: One identified component offered by one actor to one client in one promotional context at one assessment time.

unresolved: Both prior models already preserve component separation, product-type promotion and offering-time assessment. The source does not support inventing additional temporal or product-scope rivals.

The offeror/provider distinction is consequential only if 'provider' in the prior model means funder or fulfiller. If it means offeror, the proposed correction clarifies the vocabulary rather than establishing a different legal reading.

The words 'any gifts' require coverage of every relevant component before a negative whole-offer conclusion. A known finite inventory permits a disjunction of component results; an unspecified inventory cannot be quantified over in the supplied expression fragment. What is the complete component inventory?

The source does not supply exhaustive gift or discount definitions, the referenced FAQ answer, or a complete attribution test for third-party benefits. These remain judgment questions rather than assigned truths.
No actual offer facts are supplied. Legal completeness, equivalence of the prior models and compliance with separate restrictions remain unestablished.
